stem: Species such as $\text{NH}_4^+$, $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ and $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ are examples of molecular ions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Ionic and covalent bonds both involve an electrostatic attraction between different species.

Identify the species that are electrostatically attracted to one another in:

- an ionic bond

- a covalent bond.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Complete Table 1.1 to show the total numbers of protons and electrons in the molecular ions $\text{NH}_4^+$, $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ and $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$.

Table 1.1

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
When $\text{NH}_4^+\text{(aq)}$ is heated with $\text{NaOH(aq)}$, a pungent gas is produced.

Write an ionic equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
The nitrogen atom in $\text{NH}_4^+$ is $\text{sp}^3$ hybridised. $\text{sp}^3$ orbitals form from the mixing of one 2s and three 2p orbitals.

Sketch the shapes of a 2s and a $2\text{p}_x$ orbital on the axes in Fig. 1.1.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 1.1

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: There are many naturally occurring hydrated compounds that contain the anion $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Struvite is a soft hydrated mineral with $M_r = 245.3$. The anhydrous form of the mineral has the formula $\text{NH}_4\text{MgPO}_4$.

Calculate the number of molecules of water of crystallisation in struvite.

Give your answer to the nearest integer. Show your working.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: $\text{OH}^-\text{(aq)}$ reacts with 2-bromo-2-methylpropane in an $S_N1$ reaction. The molecular ion $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}^+$ forms as the intermediate in this reaction.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text:
Draw the mechanism for the $S_N1$ reaction of $\text{OH}^-$ with 2-bromo-2-methylpropane. Include charges, dipoles, lone pairs of electrons and curly arrows as appropriate. Draw the structures of the organic reactant and organic product.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
2-bromo-2-methylpropane is a tertiary bromoalkane.

Define tertiary bromoalkane.
